title: An optional Design of DroneGo
award_status: MCM outstanding paper in the supplied 2019 special-award corpus

source_quality.notes: All 23 physical PDF pages were read in order and visually reviewed through six byte-bounded page contact sheets and two focused crops. Ordinary text extraction preserves most prose and equations but omits many table cells, splits mathematical tokens, corrupts a few glyphs, and exposes two unresolved Equation (??) references. Exact table values are retained only when confirmed by prose or focused visual review; the running team header is excluded from author evidence.

context_sources: official 2019 MCM Problem B statement, all six pages read
summary sheet, complete 22-page report body, references, CEO memo, and Figure 11 attachment
drone, cargo bay, medicine, container, map, road, population, harbor, altitude, hospital, and camera sources invoked by the paper

task_reconstruction.summary: Design a transportable DroneGo disaster-response system that packs drones, bays, and medicines into ISO cargo containers; selects fleet configurations and container drop sites; schedules medicine delivery; surveys damaged roads; balances transport and reconnaissance; and communicates a conditional Puerto Rico plan to HELP's CEO.
inputs: drone types A-H with dimensions, packed volume, speed, no-cargo flight time, payload, and camera capability
two cargo bays, three medicine packages with dimensions, weight, and anticipated daily demand, and cargo-container geometry
Puerto Rico hospitals, medical needs, roads, highways, population, harbors, altitude, and geographic grids
AHP pairwise judgments plus alpha, beta, lambda, one-third demand, and r0 feature-update premises
outputs: nested medicine-bay and drone/bay/container packing configurations with TC, Days, TCI, and RCI comparisons
one or more container drop points and drone fleet mixtures conditional on lambda
hospital-specific B/E/G payload schedules that maximize the minimum medicine-supply duration
individual and fleet routes, road-reconnaissance coverage, AHP sensitivity, and a CEO-facing system/software recommendation

section_map.summary: title: name a configurable relief-system design; handoff to abstract and roadmap
abstract: compress need, five model stages, results, robustness claim, and CEO advice; handoff to body and CEO memo
memo: translate the pipeline into CEO-facing system options; handoff to HELP decision and software prototype
introduction: move from disaster context to four promised deliverables; handoff to assumptions
problem-restatement: recast the prompt as a transport-and-reconnaissance system; handoff to scope premises and packing
assumptions: justify operational and geometric simplifications; handoff to packing and range equations
notation: define sets, indicators, coordinates, and orientation matrix; handoff to packing constraints
problem-analysis: decompose packing and geospatial decisions before optimization; handoff to data construction and equations
data-preprocessing: turn maps and specifications into normalized features and capability indices; handoff to AHP aggregation
model-establishment: build the packing-to-siting-to-schedule staircase; handoff to algorithms and results
model-improvement: replace exhaustive or single-site procedures with bounded heuristics and multi-site updates; handoff to case results
algorithm: make placement, sampling, allocation, and greedy routing executable; handoff to result tables and maps
results: report capability, packing, location, schedule, and coverage outputs; handoff to sensitivity and conclusion
sensitivity-analysis: test AHP-weight perturbations before making a robustness claim; handoff to strengths and limitations
strengths: summarize tractability, breadth, and configurability; handoff to limitations
limitations: bound solution quality, delivery policy, and data accuracy; handoff to conclusion and extension
conclusion: reassemble system, principal comparisons, outcomes, and user control; handoff to references and CEO memo
references: separate background, geography, and map-source roles; handoff to memo and reproducibility work

assumptions.summary: No charging or generating equipment is packed even though the reported deployment outcome spans more than two months.
Payload weight is assumed not to reduce maximum flight distance.
Every container carries one tethered H drone for emergency communications.
Each flight carries at most one intact top-loaded bay to one delivery location.
Helicopters can deliver cargo containers to any chosen disaster-area location.
Drone communication and data transmission are always available through radio or satellite.
Range equals 0.9 times no-cargo speed times flight time, with weather, battery, and motor variation neglected.
All containers, drones, bays, and medicine packages are treated as cuboids under orthogonal parallel placement.
At most two medicine types are placed in any one bay.
Reconnaissance uses 20-meter height, unlimited lens swing, a two-megapixel 1080P camera, and one-meter road resolution.
Each selected container is assumed to satisfy one-third of total medicine demand when supplies allow.
Already surveyed road-feature values are multiplied by r0=0.1 before selecting the next container.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Prompt-supplied drone dimensions, packed volumes, speeds, no-cargo flight times, payload capacities, and camera availability feed packing, TCI, range, and RCI interfaces.
Three medicine package dimensions, weights, and daily demands feed bay feasibility, TC, hospital weighting, and schedule constraints.
Two bay dimensions and the cargo-container interior geometry define nested three-dimensional packing domains.
Camera height, assumed 1080P/two-megapixel resolution, and one-meter road-detection resolution produce the 79.7-meter viewing-radius claim.
Main highways, all roads, population density, high-population areas, harbor distance, altitude, and hospital/medicine need are rasterized as seven feature layers.
Every feature map is normalized to unit total before it enters TI_detail or RI_detail.
The normalized medicine-demand vector (0.2949, 0.2681, 0.4369) weights hospital need.
Distances from candidate container cells to feature cells are truncated at each drone type's DIS value.
Two displayed pairwise-comparison matrices supply separate AHP group weights for transport and reconnaissance.
Tables 3-4 bind selected container coordinates and drone-volume proportions to lambda scenarios, though ordinary extraction omits most cells.
Hospital-specific daily medicine vectors and available B/E/G counts parameterize the max-min schedule.
A road target set, hospital targets, medicine-specific residual demand, and remaining drone range parameterize greedy routing.

models.summary: MU-B-2019-1908286-001: Enumerate cargo orientation and residual-space cut order, then recurse over the three new spaces.
MU-B-2019-1908286-002: Assign every typed good to one box, choose an orthogonal orientation, and keep it within box bounds.
MU-B-2019-1908286-003: Enumerate medicine combinations that fit one bay geometrically and do not exceed the carrying drone's payload.
MU-B-2019-1908286-004: Convert per-bay medicine combinations into daily packed volume, sustainable days, and a normalized drone-type transport index.
MU-B-2019-1908286-005: Choose counts of E and G transport drones, matching Bay 2 units, and one H drone to maximize payload capacity inside a container.
MU-B-2019-1908286-006: Search the heterogeneous container state space from a feasible packing when exhaustive traversal is treated as impractical.
MU-B-2019-1908286-007: Infer the maximum road-viewing radius from flight height, one-meter ground resolution, and an assumed angular pixel resolution.
MU-B-2019-1908286-008: Create seven unit-sum feature surfaces and a medicine-weighted hospital layer for siting.
MU-B-2019-1908286-009: Score how a drone type at a candidate container location serves every feature cell for transport or reconnaissance.
MU-B-2019-1908286-010: Aggregate seven detail surfaces under separate transport and reconnaissance weights and normalize drone reconnaissance capability.
MU-B-2019-1908286-011: Derive separate feature-group weights for transport and reconnaissance and screen pairwise matrices for consistency.
MU-B-2019-1908286-012: For each candidate location, choose the fleet volume mixture that maximizes a lambda-weighted product of aggregate TI and RI.
MU-B-2019-1908286-013: Select later container locations after reducing medical demand and road value served by earlier selections.
MU-B-2019-1908286-014: Enumerate B/E/G medicine combinations whose total weight fits the payload but cannot accept even the lightest additional package.
MU-B-2019-1908286-015: Allocate fixed drones and payload schemes across hospitals to maximize the minimum supply duration.
MU-B-2019-1908286-016: Use residual range after delivery to survey the nearest unsearched road segments and remove them from future targets.
MU-B-2019-1908286-017: Coordinate drones by serving medicine-specific demand, prioritizing short-range reconnaissance opportunities, and dedicating Drone B to survey.
MU-B-2019-1908286-018: Change the largest TI or RI AHP weight and proportionally renormalize the other criteria before rerunning the location model.

dependency_graph.handoff: Recursive space states and orthogonal orientations motivate the multi-goods assignment interface.
Packing assignment, orientation, and containment constraints are specialized to MEDs and bays.
Feasible MED-bay combinations become the TC matrix consumed by sustainable-days scoring.
TCI retains E and G as transport candidates for payload-maximizing container packing.
Three-space feasibility evaluates every E/G/H/Bay-2 container arrangement.
Feasible container counts and TLW define the Monte Carlo search state and objective.
Camera radius sets the order of magnitude of the spatial grid used by feature maps.
Normalized feature surfaces are convolved with drone-location kernels.
TCI supplies the vehicle transport-capability factor in TI_alpha.
Feature-specific TI_detail and RI_detail surfaces are aggregated by AHP weights.
Separate AHP weight vectors determine the feature aggregation for TI and RI.
Drone-type TI and RI surfaces enter the fleet mixture and overall efficiency objective.
The best current single location is selected before medical and road features are updated.
Updated medical and road surfaces define the next single-location optimization.
Medicine weights and payload limits constrain the satisfactory B/E/G scheme sets.
Selected container fleets and nearby hospital demands parameterize the schedule.
Full-payload scheme sets K_i are allocated across delivery locations.
Each drone's assigned medicine and hospital target initializes its individual route.
Individual delivery-first routes and deleted road targets feed fleet coordination.
RCI and range differences motivate fleet reconnaissance priority and B specialization.
Baseline AHP weights are the direct sensitivity inputs.
Perturbed and renormalized weights trigger a complete location and mixture rerun.

results_trace.summary: The source reports the seven-by-three TC matrix produced by feasible medicine-bay combinations.
The Days vector is reported as approximately (2.97, 15.92, 8.78, 24.45, 41.46, 28.98, 47.21), making G the normalized TCI leader and E second.
Table 1 reports satisfactory container configurations with space utilization up to 97.97 percent and an approximately 106-day transport-capability interpretation.
The packing result is presented as consistent with Drone G's independent TCI ranking.
The camera equations report theta=1.322 rad and r_view=79.7 m, then round this into a roughly 100-meter grid.
The RCI vector reports Drone B at 1.0000 while every other type is below 0.19.
AHP assigns 67.03 percent of the transport group weight to medical information and 60.11 percent of the reconnaissance group weight to highway information.
Figure 7 presents different single-location solutions for lambda values 0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0.
Tables 3-4 report sequential multi-location selections and their lambda dependence; the lambda=0.5 case supplies the downstream schedule and route plan.
The source reports 3, 27, and 44 satisfactory medicine payload schemes for B, E, and G.
Table 5 reports a payload and schedule configuration returned by the integer program.
Figure 10 reports 59.86 percent Puerto Rico road reconnaissance coverage for the three-container lambda=0.5 case.
The conclusion states more than two months of medicine delivery and nearly 60 percent road coverage under equal transport-reconnaissance emphasis.

contributions.summary: Turns one cuboid placement into an explicit orientation-by-cut-order residual-space recursion before generalizing to heterogeneous goods.
Separates geometric packing, payload feasibility, space utilization, and medicine transport capacity rather than treating container volume as the only constraint.
Defines an interpretable duration-based TCI that screens drone types before expensive container search.
Moves from unknown-location transport capacity to geography-aware reconnaissance only after a feasible fleet configuration exists.
Factorizes each spatial score into distance, coverage-area normalization, drone capability, and geographic feature mass.
Uses separate AHP judgments for transport and reconnaissance, retaining their distinct operational priorities.
Exposes stakeholder preference through lambda after TI and RI are constructed, allowing alternative configurations and locations.
Recognizes diminishing marginal value across multiple containers by updating served medical and road features after every selection.
Connects full-payload medicine schemes to a max-min hospital service objective and individual drone payload outputs.
Makes delivery priority, nearest-road search, duplicate-road deletion, short-range priority, and Drone B specialization explicit in route narration.
Rewrites the same dependency chain for a CEO and proposes a user-facing system frame rather than ending at equations alone.

writing_logic.summary: The summary starts with Hurricane Maria and HELP's response need, then advances through transport capability, reconnaissance capability, geographic siting, lambda tradeoff, multiple containers, schedule, route, and bounded case outcomes.
The introduction makes four deliverables scannable and preserves their dependency order: packing, capability-aware siting, payload configuration, and route planning.
The first technical staircase solves nested MED-to-bay and drone/bay-to-container geometry before any capability or geographic claim is made.
Feasible medicine configurations become TC, daily packed volume, Days, and TCI, which screen E and G and define the container payload objective.
After a Monte Carlo packing result, the report changes scale from physical containers to a 100-meter-order map through a camera viewing-radius argument.
Seven normalized feature layers, hospital medicine weights, distance kernels, coverage normalization, TCI, RCI, and separate AHP weights build TI and RI surfaces in an inspectable order.
Lambda enters only after separate TI and RI surfaces exist, turning a two-objective siting problem into a configurable multiplicative utility and continuous fleet mixture.
For multiple containers, each selected site changes later medical and road features; those sites and fleets then feed medicine-scheme enumeration and max-min hospital scheduling.
The fixed payload schedule becomes the priority input for individual and fleet greedy routing, whose route maps produce the 59.86 percent road-coverage claim.
The report perturbs AHP weights, separates source-authored strengths and weaknesses, reassembles the system answer, and translates it into a CEO memo and software frame.

assumption followed by operational justification: State a simplifying premise, give the physical or emergency rationale, and expose the model consequence. Occurrences=12; order=premise -> contextual reason -> simplification -> model consequence -> reality boundary; slots=[assumption]; [evidence or context]; [simplification]; [affected term]; [limitation]; variants=we assume; because; therefore; for simplicity; in reality; boundary=A plausible emergency rationale does not make the premise observed, especially for range, charging, communication, and helicopter access.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The summary's complete need-to-model-to-result chain is judge-scannable, but award status does not prove that this structure caused the outcome.
The early packing schematic and explicit residual-space narration plausibly reduce cognitive load before the integer formulation; this is a clarity hypothesis, not demonstrated judge causation.
Aligned TI/RI maps and weight diagrams make the transport-reconnaissance distinction visually immediate, subject to missing arrays and uncertainty.
Tables 3-5 link abstract preference and siting decisions to concrete fleet and medicine assignments, a plausible decision-trace advantage rather than proof of mathematical validity.
The CEO memo repeats the model dependency chain, reports case outcomes, preserves user control through lambda, and ends with a software frame, closing the stakeholder loop conditionally.

weaknesses.summary: The three-dimensional integer formulation constrains assignment, orientation, and containment but has no pairwise non-overlap constraint and no explicit nonnegative lower-coordinate bound, so geometrically intersecting goods may satisfy the printed model.

The container program cites Equation (??) twice for the bay-drone equality and one-H-per-container conditions. The prose reveals the intended relationships, but unresolved references prevent a closed, auditable printed program.
For p_hit=10^-5, the stated one-billion simulations would make 1-(1-p)^N essentially one, not 0.999954. The reported probability, exponent, and run count are numerically inconsistent.
The step from a two-megapixel/1080P camera to delta_theta=0.003 rad is underived: angular resolution also requires pixel dimensions and optical field of view, and camera/terrain effects are omitted.
DIS uses no-cargo flight time and assumes payload does not change range; it is not clear whether DIS is one-way or round-trip, so transport and reconnaissance feasibility may be overstated.

RCI uses DIS squared divided by packed drone-plus-bay volume as reconnaissance capability, but this proxy omits sensor quality, road topology, route continuity, viewing overlap, and return-flight feasibility.
The prose defines CR as the ratio CI/RI0 but then writes (lambda_max-n)/(n-1), which is the standard CI formula, as CR. Reported CI and CR values must be recomputed from the displayed matrices.
The nonlinear program optimizes continuous volume shares v(i); no integer realization constraint proves that the selected proportions fit whole drones, bays, and one tethered H inside a container.

The multi-location method is called dynamic programming, but the printed method is a sequential reweighting heuristic with assumed one-third demand reduction and no Bellman state, value recursion, or global optimality argument.

The max-min duration can exceed two months while charging/generation equipment is explicitly excluded. The schedule omits battery cycles, flight time, landing, unloading, recharging, maintenance, and replenishment constraints.
Only one AHP weight is perturbed at a time. Small local location changes do not establish strong robustness of packing, range, integer scheduling, routing, data, or the complete end-to-end decision.

TCI is a container-volume duration proxy computed with fractional equivalent drones and one homogeneous drone type; it does not validate a mixed-fleet, repeated-flight, route-time, or energy-feasible deployment.
The authors acknowledge that Monte Carlo solution quality may fall below expectation.
The authors acknowledge that the rule for distributing medicine across delivery positions is uncertain.
The authors acknowledge that conclusions depend on the accuracy of collected data and estimated geographic and medical information.
The route prose starts from delivery and consumes extra range for roads but does not close return flight, landing, unloading, charging, maintenance, communications, or battery-cycle constraints.
The paper excludes charging and generating equipment while later claiming medicine delivery for more than two months.
One tethered H drone is justified by damaged communications, while a later premise says drone communication and data transmission are always available.
Reference [2] has a drone-rescue title but a CIA factbook URL, while reference [3] has a Puerto Rico factbook title but a web-technology language URL.

independent_extensions.summary: Close the three-dimensional packing model with coordinate domains and pairwise disjunctive non-overlap, then compare recursive packing with exact CP-SAT or MILP bounds.
Publish the complete E/G/H/Bay-2 program, repair unresolved references, freeze proposal distribution and seeds, and report incumbent traces, runtime, and optimality gaps.
Derive angular resolution from sensor pixels and field of view, then calibrate road-detection probability against altitude, terrain, blur, lighting, and occlusion.
Freeze all seven rasters, source versions, coordinate reference system, cell resolution, missingness, normalization, hospital joins, and provenance hashes.
Recompute both AHP matrices, elicit judgments from multiple stakeholders, report disagreement, and compare AHP with data-driven or robust weight intervals.
Enumerate feasible integer container compositions and show their nondominated TI-RI frontier instead of optimizing continuous volume shares alone.
Replace sequential one-third/r0 reweighting with a joint multi-site facility-location and coverage model, then quantify the heuristic gap.
Add time-indexed demand, battery inventory, charge or replacement logistics, flight cycles, loading/unloading, maintenance, and uncertainty to the max-min schedule.
Formulate delivery-and-survey routing as an energy-constrained multi-depot orienteering/vehicle-routing problem with launch, return, service, communication, and safe-terminal states.
Run global and joint sensitivity over geometry, demand, range, camera, feature data, AHP judgments, lambda, r0, fleet counts, solver randomness, schedule, and route decisions.
Repair reference-title/URL mismatches, archive exact source bytes, and independently verify every external specification and geographic claim.
Implement the software frame with typed interfaces, provenance, scenario comparison, uncertainty, accessibility, operator override, failure modes, tests, and an audit trail.
